newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London recovered much of the day's losses in the afternoon helped by small gains in New York, but the market still ended slightly down. November remained unchanged at $1,572 per tonne, while January lost $3 to close at $1,422 per tonne. The November contract was supported by light short-covering activity ahead of its expiry this Friday.

In New York arabica futures were lower across the board. December lost 50 points to close at 117.75 cents/lb while March gave up 1.90 cents/lb to close at 107.60 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 1.85 to 3.75 cents/lb. Traders expect to see book-squaring this week in view of the long weekend. The market will be closed Thursday and Friday for the Thanksgiving holiday.

UNITED STATES - The CSCE said certified coffee stocks remained unchanged at 321 bags during the week ended November 22. This will not come as a surprise to the market as the stocks have been virtually nil and the 1,250 bags of coffee pending grading by the exchange have apparently disappeared. There are now no bags pending grading.

UNITED STATES - For the week ended November 16, coffee roastings totalled about 370,000 60-kg bags, up from 365,000 bags the prior week and from 330,000 in the corresponding week a year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totaled 15.250 million bags versus 14.715 million the same year-ago period.

BRAZIL - Mauricio Assis, the head of the Primary Commodity's Department of the Industry and Commerce Ministry said that Brazilian coffee exports should total around 1.5 million bags a month during November and December. Assis added that with these numbers, Brazil expected to ship around 9 million bags in the July to December period, in line with the ACPC export limitations.

Exporters have already begun to express concern over supply in the following six months (January to June) when Brazil has been allotted a further 6 million bags for exports. Trade sources said that to ship 6 million bags will have to involve strict co-ordination between the coffee community and the government. Another factor is the growing expectation of a smaller coffee harvest in 1997/98 recently estimated by Brazilian sources at 17.3-17.8 million bags against 24.5 million bags harvested in 1996/97. To increase supplies, the government has the possibility to increase the size of sales of government stocks which currently have a monthly limit of 200,000 bags but which so far have been for much smaller quantities. Assis said that the size of auctions would only be decided nearer to the time of each sale but already some exporters feel that even 200,000 bags a month will not be enough.

FRANCE - France imported 474,758 bags of coffee in August 1996, nearly 9 percent more than was imported the same month the previous year. This brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 4.494 million bags, 7.4 percent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 5.5 percent to 6.246 million bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/August 1996 were Ivory Coast (525,300 vs 495,800 bags), Uganda (359,900 vs 259,800 bags) and Brazil (453,300 vs 591,400 bags). The country exported 797,400 bags of coffee in Janaury/August 1996, 18 percent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 7.4 percent to 1.074 million bags.
